scope: Audit of the proposed frequency-rank LEB128 codec against the FaBC excerpt; local codec/byte/correctness evidence only. No distributed speedup, GPU-link throughput, energy, convergence, or task-quality claim is licensed.
source_status: The proposal and author results are not independently replicated; the supplied methods are excerpts, not a complete implementation specification.

findings.finding: The proposal treats frequency rank as if it were already a trainer-compatible node ID. A rank-coded stream needs a rank-to-original-node/trainer-index dictionary, its serialization, transfer or residency policy, and lookup cost. HaSyn's frequency sort does not establish that FaBC's codec or the trainer remaps IDs.
findings.scope_effect: Without charging the mapping and any trainer-side remap, the proposed byte ratio and decode comparison are incomplete. A local test can measure dictionary bytes, lookup time, and whether the decoded sequence exactly restores trainer IDs; it cannot infer distributed transfer savings.

findings.finding: The proposal correctly flags an ambiguity but does not freeze a baseline. 'Largest k satisfying' can mean greedy stop at first failed marginal test or global largest satisfying index; because the condition need not be monotone, these are different FaBC baselines. The source also conflicts on bitmap extent, so both k interpretations and both byte models must be reported before comparing varints.
findings.scope_effect: The cheapest valid test is analytic replay from a frozen histogram: enumerate all k, show the chosen k under each interpretation, and compute fully specified serialized bytes. Do not call a result a win until the baseline variant is declared.

findings.finding: The proposal says uniform graphs are an excluded regime, but the source only says HaSyn is most effective when updates are skewed; it does not exclude FaBC or justify removing uniform data from the main codec test. Uniform/low-skew inputs are a required counterexample and should be included as a prespecified failure regime, not silently discarded.
findings.scope_effect: Retain low-skew graphs in the held-out set and report them separately. A failure there bounds applicability; it does not refute a skew-conditional hypothesis. Do not generalize from YouTube-like skew.

findings.finding: The proposed throughput gates are unsupported by the excerpts and are not a feasible local proxy for the stated link claim. 'at least 0.5x' and 'nominal 25 GB/s link' are arbitrary choices; the energy source measures GH200/JUPITER hardware with instrumented CPU/GPU paths, not Apple GPU varint kernels or PCIe/NVLink transfer.
findings.scope_effect: Remove the 0.5x and 25 GB/s kill gates. Measure codec encode/decode wall time on the actual available device (and state CPU versus Metal/GPU implementation), bytes per decoded trainer ID, and round-trip equality. Any link-time conclusion remains an explicit model extrapolation, not a measurement.

recommended_bounded_test.operator: Known rank dictionary plus LEB128 codec, with dictionary bytes and remap work charged; FaBC baseline fixed to explicitly enumerated Eq. 8 and bitmap-length variants.
recommended_bounded_test.matched_control: Identical walks, seeds, frozen first-round histogram, trainer-ID outputs, and serialization framing; vary only codec and required rank dictionary.
metrics: encode/decode time on the Mac implementation actually used
recommended_bounded_test.kill_rule: Reject the codec if its charged bytes are not lower than the selected FaBC baseline on the prespecified skewed test, or if remapping/decoding breaks exact equality; report low-skew results as applicability bounds, not as an excluded omission.
